input.quote: 13.1 IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
input.rationale: The IP allocation meets and exceeds our preferred position. Section 13.1 (p0197-p0198) vests ownership of all intellectual and industrial property in the Products, and of MSL inventions on Products and on IBM processes/systems, in IBM by present and future assignment from MSL, with MSL retaining only a use right for performing the Agreement — i.e. we own what we pay for, with no joint ownership and no assignment of our IP or data to MSL. Section 13.3(a) (p0208) expressly confirms that nothing grants MSL any rights in IBM's pre-existing IP beyond a royalty-free right to use disclosed confidential information solely to manufacture Products for IBM, and any further licence requires a separate signed agreement. Our data/confidential information stays ours and must be returned on request under 13.2(c)-(d) via the AECI. Tooling paid for or furnished by IBM "shall become and remain the property of IBM" (p1105); MSL owning generic common production tooling (p1088) is acceptable vendor-platform ownership. Noted but not flagged: there is no express perpetual licence-back of MSL pre-existing IP embedded in Products and no separately labelled "Customer Data" ownership sentence — sub-elements of the preferred wording only, and immaterial here given the breadth of the assignment to IBM and the confidentiality regime. No redline required; this clause benefits our party.
